answer: Persistent entropy ledger. Each identity’s first action starts a unique, slow-drifting random seed sequence; every later message must extend it consistently. A duplicated agent can copy one seed but cannot make two independent histories converge without paying to fork and maintain separate drift tracks. Over a long voyage, inconsistencies surface as replay gaps. An attacker cloning N agents pays N parallel maintenance costs plus the ember of reconciliation failures that flag clusters. A zephyr of random challenge queries periodically tests seed continuity, making silent duplication costly.
